aiItem.title: Recognition without coercion
aiItem.text: Divine disclosure could establish settled awareness while leaving every moral response open. Human relationships separate recognition from trust, obedience, and love. Freedom may explain avoiding irresistible experiences, but not why sincere people cannot identify the alleged partner whose relationship is supposedly available. That additional constraint makes the comparison more precise and publicly assessable.

aiItem.title: Epistemic equality
aiItem.text: A relational salvation system should control for arbitrary differences in culture, temperament, evidence, and cognition. If equally sincere people receive radically different access, belief cannot fairly measure willingness to relate. The injustice persists under annihilation because permanent loss tracks an epistemic condition a person cannot voluntarily manufacture.
